question: What role does oxygen play in suppressing the redox route of water dissociation on gadolinium oxide surfaces?
answer: Oxygen suppresses the redox route of water dissociation on gadolinium oxide surfaces by diffusing into the gadolinium bulk during heat treatment under high vacuum, creating oxygen vacancies in the native oxide layer. These vacancies influence the adsorption and dissociation behavior of water vapor, as evidenced by XPS, XRD, and AFM analyses, which showed reduced hydride formation and differences in surface morphology when oxygen is present compared to an argon atmosphere.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate the effect of oxygen on the dissociation of water vapor on gadolinium oxide (GdO1.5) surfaces, focusing on the interplay between ionic dissociation and redox mechanisms. The study combines experimental methods and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate how oxygen influences the formation of hydrides on oxide-coated metals by suppressing the redox route of water dissociation.
